paragraphs.text: Independent typed decisions and a durable task / multi-device execution suite for DeepSeek Harness,
with optional channel adapters and WebUI.
# DSH Orchestration
Configurable task management mounted inside DeepSeek Harness. A stable task keeps multiple runs, ses
sions, reports, revisions and artifacts. User-defined templates and schedules use the same ledger an
d lifecycle. Planner, executor and combined roles compose through explicit permissions and authentic
ated peer protocols.
This monorepo targets **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2** and **Node 24+**. The TLS fixture test also us
es the system OpenSSL executable. All plugins attach to a DSH host; an external supervisor may keep
that host alive. The plugins do not install their own OS services or manage platform updates.
## Core plugins and optional adapter
| Package | Independent use inside DSH |
| Task and Remote Execution Suite | Durable task configuration, history, execution, observation, sch

eduling and optional authenticated remote peers; useful without decisions or channels |
| JEV shared
model service | Provider/model management and typed calls for any consumer; System One APIs and ord

inary models through DSH |
| Optional Feishu adapter | Separate optional channel SDK and authorized

chat/message delivery; replaceable through public consumer/delivery contracts |
| WebUI | Portable r
ead-only consumer of the same TaskLedger, with timestamped private snapshot export |
The active installation packages are `dsh-jev-plugin` and `@dsh-task/task-system`; the task suite is
useful without a model service. Remote coordination ships inside the task suite and is explicitly m
ounted through its `/remote` export. Feishu is an optional adapter. See the boundary and upstream re
use assessment and JEV replacement migration.
Role profiles, protocol types, task templates and the WebUI are not presented as extra dependency-on
ly runtime plugins. Plugin independence means useful installation and lifecycle within a host, not a
s. Plugin independence means useful installation and lifecycle within a host, not a separate daemon.
## Build and verify
Develop on a feature branch from `dev`, then open a PR to `dev`. Before release, verify a fixed dev
SHA with full CI, test its retained packages on real devices, and obtain explicit user confirmation.
Prepare package versions once per formal release before testing; ordinary feature PRs do not each b
ump versions. The release workflow fast-forwards `main` to the tested SHA and derives its version ta
g. Detailed acceptance stays in Actions artifacts; the tag contains a short summary and CI link. Fol
low the development and release workflow before changing code or integrating a PR.

`check` builds the task suite and runs the core ledger/protocol, native DSH integration, UI contract
s, official runtime, JEV, read-only dashboard, shipped task packs and management tests. It prepares
an isolated pinned DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 installation for the official tests. The mandatory browser checks
exercise real React settings, executor reminders and polling text selection; distribution checks ins
tall, boot and remove the built core packages while verifying retained data. GitHub runs these suite
s in separate jobs, with Linux checks on daily PRs, Linux/macOS core and native checks for a release
candidate, and UTC browser coverage. See CI coverage and commands.
The default build and checks do not build, test, install or distribute Feishu. Its source and option
al entries remain available:

Tests use disposable local records, credentials and deterministic model fixtures. They do not requir
e live Feishu/JEV/model calls or production machines. No CI job deploys to a device.
For a runnable offline native example, see the DSH integration guide and `tests/dsh/demo-local.mjs`.
It uses a deterministic model fixture, visibly labeled as such.

## One ledger and explicit evidence
Point both `DSH_TASK_DATABASE` and the WebUI `--ledger` setting at the intended database. The privat
e development instance uses `.runtime/tasks.sqlite`, excluded from Git and package artifacts. Static
exports carry their observation cutoff and stale status; they do not claim to synchronize all inter
nal agents automatically.
Observed work is captured before admission and never dispatched merely because it was observed. A se
parately authorized new request can continue an existing objective while retaining its prior evidenc
e. Task results, report validity, partial-review status, finalized artifacts and message delivery re
s, report validity, partial-review status, finalized artifacts and message delivery remain distinct.
Cancelling a run does not cancel other runs of the same task. Cancellation resources remain held unt
il actual quiescence is acknowledged. Uncertain effects require reconciliation; restart never blindl
y resends a workload. Similar reports remain separate records, while exact operation replay returns
the original receipt.
## Configure and extend
Example task types show daily review, game-daily and a third unrelated workflow using one template/s
chema contract. Define source adapters, normalization, validation and presentation through reviewed
host code; task configuration selects capabilities but does not grant credentials or executable perm
e; task configuration selects capabilities but does not grant credentials or executable permissions.
Workspace provisioning creates actual directories under explicit roots. Model answers can recommend
reuse or creation, but physical provisioning and final execution policy remain deterministic host re
sponsibilities. Host delegation illustrates optional local specialist/Codex delegation without a ded
icated backend or self-maintenance plugin.
